newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila plans to cut long dlr position of banks.
newsitem.headline: Manila plans to cut long dlr position of banks.

text.p: The Philippine central bank's decision-making monetary board plans to cut the long dollar position of banks, Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP) president Deogracias Vistan said on Wednesday.
At its meeting later in the day, the board will consider cutting long dollar positions to five percent from 10 percent, or to $10 million, whichever is lower, Deogracias told Reuters.
The dollar positions are computed based on a bank's capital.
"We have been advised by the central bank that we should expect some changes in the regulations of foreign exchange transactions," Vistan said.
Another proposed change is to lower the limit to $25,000 from $100,000 for over-the-counter dollar sales to individuals, he said.
On the plan to cut the long dollar positions, Vistan said bankers were generally open to the idea after he held a meeting earlier with other members of the BAP.
"They feel it is reasonable and again the idea is to discourage people from holding them (dollars) without using them productively, " he said.

On the over-the counter dollar sales limit, Vistan said: "It's not a question of controls but it's just a possible leakage because $100,000 is quite substantial and it's like an open invitation for anybody to buy and speculate. So close that."
The central bank has been changing regulations on currency trading for banks to stem speculation.
The peso, which was effectively devalued over two weeks ago, had been hit by currency turmoil in the region caused by Thailand's financial woes.
